transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Start: 15:00 UTC (08:00 PT)
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alicia (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Priya (CSM), Marc (CTO - Stonybridge), Lina (Platform Eng), Samir (Security), Hannah (SRE)

---- Optional auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough) ----
This was the implementation kickoff / handoff from sales to CS/SE. High-level goals: pilot readiness, network prep, encryption/KMS review, and cadence for the two-week pilot. We covered risk points: data residency, egress, and canary fallback. Action items and owners captured at the end.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alicia (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alicia from Redwood Inference, AE on the account. Quick intros then we'll hand over to Jordan for the technical checklist.
[00:18] Marc (Stonybridge): Hi, Marc here, CTO. We're excited to get this moving, want a short runway to pilot before end of month.
[00:25] Lina (Stonybridge): Lina, platform eng, I'll own the cluster side and network config.
[00:29] Samir (Stonybridge): Samir, security, will be validation for encryption and audit logs.
[00:34] Jordan (Redwood SE): Jordan, SE. We'll walk through the deployment playbook and known pitfall list.
[00:40] Priya (Redwood CSM): Priya, CSM, I'll coordinate go-live readiness and comms.
[01:02] Jordan (Redwood SE): OK, first slide — overview of deployment modes. For the pilot you mentioned wanting predictability, so we're proposing a dedicated pool in your VPC with private control plane. A couple notes: we'll need peering, outbound rules for image pulls, and KMS access if you want us to use customer-managed keys.
[01:26] Marc (Stonybridge): Peering is fine, we have strict egress filters. Who will initiate the peering, us or Redwood?
[01:33] Alicia (Redwood): We typically have the customer do the VPC side and we provide the peering details and routes — less friction from a compliance angle.
[01:42] Samir (Stonybridge): For KMS, we prefer HSM-backed keys. Is Redwood able to integrate with customer KMS/HSM via IAM roles?
[01:50] Jordan (Redwood SE): Short answer yes, we support customer-managed KMS via cross-account roles. There might be a small token exchange for signing. We'll send the IAM policy snippet. (mumble) that said, if you prefer Redwood-managed KMS, we can do that too but obviously less control.
[02:18] Lina (Stonybridge): Any special ports that need opening? Our infra team is strict on egress.
[02:25] Jordan (Redwood SE): Primarily outbound to our artifact registry and control-plane endpoints on TLS 443. Also the model pull step may momentarily reach out to model storage endpoints. We'll document exact IP ranges; we can also do a temporary allowlist for the pilot window.
[02:41] Hannah (Stonybridge SRE): What's the expected bandwidth during a spike? We run bursts during peak logistic batches.
[02:49] Jordan (Redwood SE): Depends on request size and batching — if you run 512-token average with continuous batching at 5 concurrent connectors, rough outbound ~100 Mbps — but we'll run the sample workload and give you numbers.
[03:10] Marc (Stonybridge): Okay, pilot success criteria — we need 99th percentile under 300ms for single-turn prompts and cost under our target threshold. Can Redwood promise that?
[03:22] Alicia (Redwood): We'll operate to SLOs in the Dedicated tier; can set a canary model with lower latency profile. Jordan will validate with your sample payloads. Not a legal SLA until we sign Dedicated contract, but we'll aim for the target during the pilot.
[03:38] Samir (Stonybridge): SOC2 reports — do you provide a compressed package or do we have to go through the portal? Also audit logs: retention and schema?
[03:47] Priya (Redwood CSM): We can share SOC2 summary and the security pack. Audit logs are available via the Console with configurable retention; default 90 days, longer retained for enterprise add-on. We'll include schema samples in the pack.
[04:02] Marc (Stonybridge): Data residency — some of our payloads are EU-only. Can the pilot use Europe region?
[04:10] Jordan (Redwood SE): Yes, we can route the pilot to eu-west and pin model variants there. There's a small latency delta but it meets residency. We'll show region routing options in the playbook doc.
[04:33] Lina (Stonybridge): How does KV cache and prefix caching interact with our privacy needs? We don't want customer data stored in a shared cache.
[04:42] Jordan (Redwood SE): Good question — for dedicated pools we spin up isolated KV cache instances per tenant, not shared. There was a past doc that referred to 'K V cash' in a demo transcript, sorry the ASR mangled it. We'll include technical notes and cache TTL defaults.
[05:05] Marc (Stonybridge): What's the rollback plan if a new model variant causes quality regression?
[05:10] Priya (Redwood CSM): We support canary rollouts and instant fallback to previous pinned model. We'll define rollout percentages and health thresholds.
[05:28] Jordan (Redwood SE): On instrumentation: we'll provide token-level cost breakdowns, request tracing headers, and per-model metrics in the Console. For the pilot, we can stream the metrics to your Prometheus if you prefer.
[05:46] Hannah (Stonybridge SRE): Prometheus push is ideal. Any existing exporters?
[05:50] Jordan (Redwood SE): Yes, we'll hand over a prometheus exporter config and example scrape job.
[06:12] Marc (Stonybridge): Timeline — you mentioned a two-week pilot? We want to start network prep this week if possible.
[06:19] Alicia (Redwood): Sounds good. We can aim to start the pilot by 2026-10-13 if network and KMS are ready. That gives us a one-week prep and then two-week pilot.
[06:31] Samir (Stonybridge): Who will have access to audit logs — read-only for security, admin for ops?
[06:36] Priya (Redwood CSM): We'll set RBAC roles: Security (read-only audit), Platform (admin read/write), Product (metrics only). We'll draft the RBAC matrix and include it in the security pack.
[06:56] Marc (Stonybridge): Pricing questions — if we go Dedicated for pilot, is there an overage mechanism?
[07:03] Alicia (Redwood): For pilots we do a short-term reserved pool with a soft cap. Overage is charged at the reserved rate plus a small premium; appendix will show estimates. We'll send a sample invoice model.
[07:22] Lina (Stonybridge): Any code changes required on our side or just network and auth?
[07:27] Jordan (Redwood SE): Minimal code changes — mostly config. We'll provide an SDK snippet and a sample request template; if you need function/tool calling or structured outputs, there may be parsing integrations but not necessary for basic inference.
[07:46] Marc (Stonybridge): OK, security will need the legal/data processing agreement.
[07:51] Alicia (Redwood): We'll attach the DPA and standard addenda. If you need a custom clause for data residency, we can escalate legal.
[08:08] Jordan (Redwood SE): Technical deep-dive — I'll go over the network checklist: NAT vs private endpoints, IP ranges, TLS cert management, and KMS roles.
[08:21] Jordan (Redwood SE): Step 1: Provide VPC diagram. Step 2: Create a cross-account role for KMS or provide a certificate for redwood-managed keys. Step 3: Allowlist our control-plane IPs. Step 4: Provide sample payloads for perf testing.
[08:54] Marc (Stonybridge): On sample payloads — we'll strip PII but keep structure. Expect 5k req/day peak for pilot.
[09:02] Jordan (Redwood SE): That's helpful. We'll run a synthetic replay to match your concurrency pattern. Expect baseline numbers back within 3 business days.
[09:28] Hannah (Stonybridge SRE): Any concerns about tokenization differences across models causing latency variability?
[09:34] Jordan (Redwood SE): We recommend picking a model family and pinning it for the pilot. Tokenization is model-specific and can change throughput; we'll annotate that in the report.
[09:55] Samir (Stonybridge): Auditability — is there a way to prove no data persisted beyond retention?
[10:00] Priya (Redwood CSM): We can provide an export of retention deletion logs as part of the audit package.
[10:12] Marc (Stonybridge): Great. Can we also get a canary plan for model rollouts?
[10:17] Jordan (Redwood SE): Yes — typical is 5/25/50/100% ramp with health checks. We'll propose thresholds for latency and error rate.
[10:36] Alicia (Redwood): Quick check — any blockers that would prevent you from starting the network work tomorrow?
[10:42] Lina (Stonybridge): We need the IAM snippet and IP ranges. Once we have that we can open a ticket and start.
[10:49] Alicia (Redwood): I'll send both today.
[11:05] Marc (Stonybridge): On metrics — we want cost per 1k tokens and 99th pct latency in the dashboard, plus a daily aggregate CSV. Can Redwood provide CSV export?
[11:12] Priya (Redwood CSM): Yes, Console allows CSV and API exports. We'll demo the export during the next call.
[11:31] Jordan (Redwood SE): Benchmarks note — our runtime supports quantization and batching; we may recommend int8 quant for cost during pilot if quality is acceptable. We'll do A/B tests.
[11:50] Marc (Stonybridge): A/B is good. We can't sacrifice quality for cost on customer-facing flows but for internal ops we can be flexible.
[11:58] Alicia (Redwood): Understood. We'll mark primary tests as customer-facing.
[12:20] Hannah (Stonybridge SRE): Any logging overhead concerns when streaming to Prometheus?
[12:25] Jordan (Redwood SE): Slight overhead for high-cardinality traces; will recommend sampling for traces and full counters for aggregates.
[12:43] Marc (Stonybridge): Ok, let's confirm dates: Alicia suggested starting pilot 2026-10-13. That works for us if we get the network docs and KMS role in the next week.
[12:52] Alicia (Redwood): Great — next steps in the notes. We'll also schedule the infra deep dive for 2026-10-08 10am PT.
[13:14] Marc (Stonybridge): Anything else from Redwood side?
[13:19] Jordan (Redwood SE): I'll run the perf test, need sample payloads and a spike profile.
[13:25] Lina (Stonybridge): We'll upload payloads to the shared drive by Friday.
[13:34] Samir (Stonybridge): We'll review the DPA and SOC2 pack when received.
[13:42] Priya (Redwood CSM): I'll create the pilot Slack channel and send invites.
[13:52] Alicia (Redwood): Recap: Redwood sends security pack, IAM snippet, IP ranges, pricing appendix; SE runs baseline perf; customer shares network diagram and sample payloads; schedule infra deep-dive 2026-10-08.
[14:10] Marc (Stonybridge): Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[14:21] Alicia (Redwood): Thanks, we'll follow up in email with attachments.
[14:30] (meeting wrap)

---- End of transcript ----
